title: When to Use PLS-SEM vs Covariance-Based CB-SEM

transcript: Welcome to Course 8: SmartPLS 4 & Structural Equation Modeling. In this opening lecture, we resolve the decisive methodological debate: When should you use Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM) and when should you use Covariance-Based SEM (AMOS / LISREL)?

Both methods belong to the second generation of multivariate data analysis, but they serve fundamentally distinct scientific philosophies. Covariance-Based SEM (CB-SEM) is a confirmatory, theory-testing technique that aims to minimize the difference between the sample covariance matrix and the theoretical covariance matrix. It strictly requires multivariate normal distributions and large sample sizes (typically N > 250).

Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM), by contrast, is a variance-based, prediction-oriented approach. It maximizes the explained variance (R-squared) of the endogenous constructs. According to Hair, Hult, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2022), PLS-SEM is the superior choice when your research goal is exploratory theory development or prediction, when models are complex with multiple mediators or moderators, when data is non-normal, or when sample sizes are small to moderate.

In Pakistan universities, business and social science dissertations frequently utilize SmartPLS because empirical survey data in emerging markets almost always departs from strict multivariate normality.
key: CB-SEM (AMOS) tests goodness-of-fit for established theories under strict multivariate normality assumptions.
PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4) maximizes explained variance (R²) for prediction and exploratory research models.
Choose PLS-SEM when models contain complex mediating/moderating paths, formative constructs, or non-normal data.
Never claim PLS-SEM 'does not need any sample size'—it still requires adequate power determined by G*Power or minimum R² rules.
